verdict: Carnival set records in its summer quarter — $8.4B of revenue and $1.9B of profit — as record bookings for 2027 outran a spike in fuel prices.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was a record $8.4B, vs $8.2B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.33 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.43, flat YoY

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: level with last year's record, $110M ahead of June guidance

kpis.label: Customer deposits
kpis.note: a third-quarter record, up nearly 7% YoY on flat capacity

segments.name: Passenger ticket
segments.note: Ticket sales — the fare passengers pay to sail. An all-time high, with net yields (revenue per berth-day, constant currency) up 2.4%.

segments.name: Onboard & other
segments.note: Spending once aboard — drinks, excursions, spas, casinos — plus tour and other revenue. The fastest-growing piece.

opex.name: Selling & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the cruise brands and running the company ashore — up 7% YoY.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the fleet and other long-lived assets over their lives — a non-cash charge.

otherDetail: Interest and other items cost $280M net: $285M of interest expense and $23M of debt-extinguishment costs, partly offset by $17M of interest income and $10M of other income.
oneTimers: Adjusted net income was $1,963M vs $1,920M GAAP (attributable) — the gap is $23M of debt extinguishment and modification costs, $8M of restructuring expense, $2M of ship-sale and impairment losses and $10M of other items the company strips out.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M, so lines may differ by $1M from the release (operating income is shown as $2,219M; the release reports $2,220M). Net income of $1,923M includes $3M earned by noncontrolling interests; $1,920M was attributable to Carnival Corporation. Cruise operating costs of $4,628M comprise commissions & transportation $988M, onboard costs $902M, other ship operating $1,081M, payroll $641M, fuel $615M and food $401M.

takeaways.title: Pricing power is real
takeaways.text: Net yields — what Carnival earns per available berth-day, in constant currency — rose 2.4% to an all-time high, more than a point ahead of guidance, on flat capacity growth.

takeaways.title: Fuel ate the upside
takeaways.text: Fuel cost $615M vs $451M a year ago — a $131M ($0.10 per share) drag with currency effects. Adjusted EPS was flat at $1.43 despite record revenue; management still lifted the full-year outlook by over $150M vs June guidance.

takeaways.title: 2027 is already selling at records
takeaways.text: Customer deposits hit a third-quarter record $7.6B, and 2027 booked occupancy and pricing are at record levels. Carnival also bought back about $1.2B of shares this year and won an S&P upgrade to investment grade.
